limits.excludedTracks: Tracks without sufficient instrumental credits are excluded from the palette calculation. Lesser-known artists and some current music, especially music made with software, may have fewer published credits: programmed, synthesized, or sampled sounds are not always listed as instruments.
limits.incompleteCredits: An instrument can be present in a song without being documented in its MusicBrainz recording credits. Finding a recording in that database does not guarantee finding its instruments. Documentation varies across repertoires, so absence from the palette does not mean absence from the music.
limits.intro: An approximate reading of your listening.
limits.method: The palette combines your public Last.fm history with published instrumental credits. It does not analyze song audio or measure instrument volume.
limits.refresh: The catalog may receive new data, so a future lookup may produce a different result, without any guarantee of identifying more instruments.
limits.temperament: Listening temperament is a playful editorial interpretation. It is not a psychological or scientific assessment of your personality.
limits.title: Analysis limitations
limits.vocabulary: Artist vocabulary brings together instruments documented in recordings by those artists; it does not confirm that they appear in the songs you listened to.

sources.method: This reading uses rules version <version>{tracks}</version> for the track palette and <version>{artists}</version> for artist vocabulary. Changes to the snapshot or these rules may also change the result.
sources.snapshot: Instrument data comes from published MusicBrainz credits. We use snapshot <version>{snapshot}</version>, a copy of those data. The project may still look up more recordings in that copy, so a future visit may reveal new credits.
